items.project_definition: The set of properties ensuring transactional reliability and data integrity for user follows and match records.
The RESTful interface used to retrieve external football data through a service layer with caching and rate limiting.
The security mechanism implemented to prevent cross-site request forgery within the authentication flow.
The styling layer implemented via a utility-first approach for rapid interface development.
The unique minimal identifier stored for users linked to third-party authentication providers.
The lightweight data-interchange format used for communicating with external football data providers.
The binary storage format in the relational database used for flexible data schemas from external sources.
The signed token format utilized for secure session management.
The baseline scripting language rejected as the primary development choice in favor of a typed alternative.
The long-term support version of the runtime environment to ensure stability and performance.
The component library following Material Design guidelines for the user interface.
The authorization framework used for third-party logins via Google, Facebook, and Apple.
The abstraction layer provided by Sequelize or TypeORM for database interactions and migrations.
The primary relational database engine version 14 used for structured match and user data.
The frontend library version 18 utilizing concurrent features and hooks for the user interface.
The static type-checked language version 4.9 used across the entire application stack.
The visual layer developed using a combination of utility-first styles or pre-built components.
